back: A tool made by local people from local materials using skills passed down through generations.
Skins attached to clay pipes, used to pump air into a furnace so it is hot enough to smelt or work iron.

front: Hoe, axe and spear in Shona and Ndebele?
back: Hoe: badza / ikhuba. Axe: demo / izembe. Spear: pfumo / umkhonto.
The mortar (duri, a hollowed log) and pestle (mutswi, a wooden pole) used to pound grain.
A deadfall trap: a heavy flat stone propped on sticks over bait, which falls on small animals.

front: Four stages of making an iron tool?
back: Mining ore → smelting with charcoal and bellows → forging (hammering) → fitting a wooden handle.

front: How was grain turned into flour with indigenous tools?
back: Pound in mortar and pestle, winnow in a rusero, grind on guyo and huyo.

front: Why do indigenous tools matter today?
back: Heritage and identity, continued rural use, ceremonies, crafts and income, education, sustainability.

front: Is hunting with snares legal today?
back: No: hunting without a permit and setting snares are illegal poaching; wildlife is protected by law.
